subject.title: fix: restrict non-owner gateway tool inventory [AI]

question: Should non-owner identity-bearing chat-driven Gateway agent turns be denied `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` even when tool allowlists include them, matching the direct Gateway tool-invocation boundary?
rationale: This is both a security-boundary fix and an upgrade-visible tool-surface restriction, so automation can review the implementation but should not decide the permanent fail-closed policy alone.

options.title: Match Direct Gateway Boundary
options.body: Apply the same owner-only rule to chat-driven agent inventories, require real behavior proof, and merge after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Keep Existing Chat Behavior
options.body: Reject or narrow this PR if non-owner chat automations are intentionally allowed to use these tools despite the direct Gateway restriction.

options.title: Add A Separate Compatibility Path
options.body: Ask for a documented migration or opt-in path if maintainers want a deprecation window before enforcing the stricter chat inventory.

recommendation.title: Match Direct Gateway Boundary
recommendation.body: Apply the same owner-only rule to chat-driven agent inventories, require real behavior proof, and merge after maintainer/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior owner-only Gateway tool-gating PR and reviewed its documented operator-facing contract.
